newsitem.title: USA: No venue change in North Carolina killings - judge.
newsitem.headline: No venue change in North Carolina killings - judge.

text.p: Superior Court Judge Robert Johnston rejected a motion on Wednesday to change the location of the murder trial of Henry Wallace, accused of killing 10 women in an alleged two-year killing spree.
Wallace will stand trial in Charlotte, where he allegedly strangled or stabbed his victims.
The trial was to start on Thursday with lawyers selecting a 12-member jury and six alternates.
"The reason for the large number of alternates is the probable length of the trial. It may last until Christmas," the judge said.
The motion requesting a change of venue claimed widespread publicity would bias potential jurors.

Wallace, 30, was arrested in March 1994. Police said that Wallace confessed on audiotape to raping and killing the women -- mainly by strangling them with their bras, T-shirts or towels -- before robbing them to support his addiction to crack cocaine.
He was to be tried on nine counts of first-degree murder, and could face a separate trial on a lesser charge for the other death.
Prosecutors Marsha Goodenow and Anne Tompkins are seeking the death penalty for each count of first-degree murder.
